About This System

Disclaimer: This is a personal, self-hosted system built for testing and learning purposes. It is provided as-is, with no warranty of any kind, express or implied. The person running this server is solely responsible for how it is used, including compliance with all applicable laws covering any content stored, streamed, downloaded, or shared through it. Whoever built or maintains this software accepts no liability for how this installation is used.
What this system does:
  • Media streaming — Jellyfin and Plex serve your video library to any device on the network (or beyond, if public access is configured).
  • Automated media management — Sonarr and Radarr track and fetch new episodes/movies, Prowlarr feeds them indexers, and Bazarr keeps subtitles in sync.
  • Downloads via a leak-proof VPN — qBittorrent, Sonarr, and Radarr are confined behind a WireGuard tunnel with a real kill-switch: if the tunnel ever drops, those three lose internet access entirely rather than falling back to your real IP.
  • Files & photos — Nextcloud handles file sync and phone photo backup with its own Photos/Memories apps.
  • Requests — Seerr lets anyone on the network request new movies/shows without needing direct access to Sonarr/Radarr.
  • Reverse proxy & public access — Caddy fronts every app under its own hostname; DuckDNS, Cloudflare Tunnel, No-IP, or Dynu can optionally expose them outside the LAN (all off by default).
  • Self-healing — a nightly routine checks jail health, network topology, the VPN tunnel, storage, and package updates, fixing what it safely can and flagging the rest right here on this dashboard.
  • This dashboard — a live status/control panel for everything above, running on a FreeBSD + KDE desktop.
